G2803.name: Claudia
G2803.desc: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
G2803.brief: Believer in Rome who sent greetings to Timothy
G2803.short: Claudia, along with others, sent greetings to Timothy in Paul's letter.

G2804G.name: Claudius
G2804G.desc: Emperor living at the time of the New Testament
G2804G.short: Claudius was the Roman emperor during part of Paul's ministry.

G2815.name: Clement
G2815.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G2815.brief: Fellow laborer with Paul in the gospel
G2815.short: Clement was a fellow laborer with Paul, whose name was in the Book of Life.

G2883.name: Cornelius
G2883.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G2883.brief: Centurion, first Gentile convert to Christianity
G2883.short: Cornelius, a centurion, was the first Gentile convert to Christianity through Peter's ministry.

G2890.name: Quartus
G2890.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G2890.brief: A Christian brother in Corinth who sent greetings to Rome
G2890.short: Quartus, a Christian brother in Corinth, sent greetings to the believers in Rome through Paul's letter.

G2802.name: Cauda
G2802.brief: Island where Paul's ship sought shelter
G2802.short: Cauda was an island where the ship carrying Paul sought shelter during a storm on his journey to Rome.

G2834.name: Cnidus
G2834.brief: City on the coast of Asia Minor
G2834.short: Cnidus was a city on the southwest coast of Asia Minor, where Paul's ship stopped during his journey to Rome.

G2857G.name: Colossae
G2857G.brief: City in Phrygia; recipient of Paul's epistle
G2857G.short: Colossae was a city in the region of Phrygia in Asia Minor, to which Paul addressed one of his epistles.

G2878.name: Corban
G2878.brief: Offering dedicated to God; temple treasury
G2878.short: Corban refers to an offering dedicated to God, which the Pharisees used to avoid supporting their parents, and also to the temple treasury.

G2882.name: Corinth
G2882.brief: Ancient Greek city; recipient of Paul's epistles
G2882.short: Corinth, an important city in ancient Greece, was the location of a Christian church to which Paul wrote two epistles.
